strengths: Well-motivated problem diagnosis with convincing diagnostic experiments (Fig. 1) clearly distinguishing router drift from expert drift
Technically sound components with rigorous derivations: spectral-aware routing, Riemannian preconditioning, and adaptive expert activation
Comprehensive ablation study (Table 2) demonstrating clear contribution of each component
Thorough analysis and insights including layer-wise routing patterns, formatting-induced forgetting discovery, and multiple validation figures
Clear presentation with well-organized methodology, informative visualizations, and algorithm boxes supporting reproducibility
Practical computational benefits from adaptive activation (32.1 min/task and 2.3 KiB/GPU reduction)
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only one benchmark (CoIN) with 8 tasks, single backbone (LLaVA-v1.5-7B), no statistical significance testing or error bars—critical limitation for ICML generalizability claims

Inadequate hyperparameter investigation: energy threshold δ, damping μ, and freezing threshold τ_score lack ablation studies; window size k not clearly specified; reproducibility and sensitivity unknown

Theoretical gaps: key assumption unvalidated (why high-variance directions equal task-relevant information?); tolerance ϵ implicitly controlled via learning rate schedule (potential confound); uncentered covariance justification weak; AGOP approximation via E[‖x‖²₂] is crude

Modest improvements with diminishing returns: 2.87% over best baseline with cumulative gains showing clear plateau (Router +10.74%, Expert +4.57%, Activation +0.93%); without confidence intervals, statistical significance unclear

Experimental design concerns: Fig. 4 fairness questionable (different gradient flow between w/ and w/o Expert); training computational overhead of covariance tracking not quantified; baseline hyperparameter tuning effort unclear
Post-hoc justification of implicit constraint absorption (Section B.3): coupling λ_t = 1/(2η_t) lacks principled motivation; learning rate effects could confound drift control improvements
Missing critical experimental details: no multi-run averaging reported, exact learning rate schedule incomplete, δ selection procedure unspecified, scalability to longer sequences (T > 8) unexplored

strengths: Well-motivated problem decomposition with compelling diagnostic evidence (Figure 1) distinguishing router drift from expert drift
Technically sound methodology combining spectral decomposition, Riemannian gradient descent, and adaptive expert freezing with rigorous mathematical derivations

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks (CoIN, UCIT, TriGap) showing consistent improvements with detailed ablation studies demonstrating complementary contributions of each component
Valuable new TriGap benchmark addressing practical challenges: extended task sequences (10 tasks), domain diversity, and non-uniform data scales
Strong reproducibility with detailed pseudocode (Algorithms 1-2), hyperparameter specifications, sensitivity analyses (Table 6), and robustness to task ordering (Tables 7-8)
Practical efficiency gains including 22% faster inference and 32.1 min/task training speedup while maintaining accuracy
Honest acknowledgment of limitations and clear presentation of both diagnostic analysis and solution design
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—spectral decomposition adapts gradient projection memory ideas, Riemannian preconditioning is established, expert freezing is conceptually straightforward; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamentally new methods
Incremental performance improvements without statistical validation: +2.08% on TriGap, +2.87% on CoIN, +1.6% on UCIT; no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests across multiple runs

Key approximations lack rigorous justification: (1) null space assumption relies on vague 'sufficiently close to 1' criterion for energy threshold δ; (2) AGOP proxy (Eq. 17) theoretically valid only for linear experts but LoRA has nonlinear routing interactions; (3) damped pseudo-inverse (Eq. 15) introduces uncharacterized approximation errors

Limited scope and generalization concerns: only LLaVA-7B tested, no evaluation on larger models; FFN-only application with unclear applicability to attention or other adaptation methods; assumes clear task boundaries; restricted to vision-language domain

Methodological inconsistencies: mixed experimental setup with some baselines reproduced and others 'directly adopted from publications'; TriGap benchmark newly constructed making verification difficult for future work; HiDe-LLaVA shows suspicious 31% performance gap between TriGap and CoIN
Sliding window averaging design (Eq. 7) appears ad-hoc with only +3.8% improvement over global averaging but no theoretical justification for why this specific form is superior

Missing statistical rigor and comparisons: no significance tests across runs; no comparison to continual learning methods outside MCIT or knowledge distillation approaches; incomplete analysis of failure modes
